documents.title: Yeshiva University Undergraduate AI Policy
documents.summary: Undergraduate AI policy of the Provost's Office. It sets a five-level framework (UG 0 to UG 4), defaults every assignment to no AI, requires written disclosure above UG 0, and sets integrity, privacy, faculty-use, assessment and governance rules.
documents.stance_why: The policy offers named tiers, so stance is delegates by the CODEBOOK rule. Its own words: "The colleges neither prohibit AI outright nor require it. Faculty decide how AI fits the learning goals of their courses", with "If no level is stated anywhere, the level is UG 0" as the fallback. The default is restrictive; unit-level codes carry that (P01, P06).

units.why: The Purpose section says preparing students for AI and protecting integrity "are the same project", an institution-level principle, so P56 (framework preamble) fits better than P44 or P95 alone.
units.anchor: preparing students for an AI-enabled world and protecting the integrity of their education are the

units.why: The sentence says AI is welcomed "where it serves learning" and limited "where it would substitute for it"; it states the dual purpose of the policy, so it is framework (P56), not a rule.
units.anchor: welcoming AI where it serves learning and drawing lines where it would substitute for it

units.why: This says the policy is "consistent with the broader policies of the University" and adds detail; it ties the AI rules to existing university policy, so P77.
units.anchor: These policies are consistent with the broader policies of the University

units.why: Plagiarism and cheating "continue to be governed by the University's existing academic integrity policies", which scopes the AI policy against existing policy (P77).
units.anchor: continue to be governed by the University's existing academic integrity policies

units.why: "The colleges neither prohibit AI outright nor require it. Faculty decide how AI fits..." hands the decision to faculty, so P04; no blanket stance (P01, P02) is set by this sentence.

units.why: The bullet commits to "clear authority and practical tools" for instructors who set AI expectations, the let-instructors-decide principle (P04).

units.why: The bullet says to help students "build the AI skills their future careers will require", a career-readiness reason (P44).
units.anchor: helping students build the AI skills their future careers will require

units.why: The bullet aims at "responsible AI fluency": using AI productively, verifying output, taking responsibility; teaching effective AI use as a skill (P44).
units.anchor: Develop responsible AI fluency appropriate to each discipline

units.why: The bullet aims to "ensure equitable access to AI tools", an equity goal (P51).
units.anchor: ensure equitable access to AI tools

units.why: "when in doubt, don't; when unsure, ask" tells students to ask before acting (P10).
units.anchor: when in doubt, don't; when unsure, ask

units.why: "unless your professor tells you in writing that you may use AI on an assignment, you may not use it" plus "When no rule is stated, the rule is no AI" states the fallback when the syllabus is silent. P06 fits better than P01 because it is about silence; the default level is coded separately.

units.anchor: Permission is never assumed. It is always granted, in writing, by your professor

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Acceptable Use Policy
documents.summary: IT policy for faculty and staff using generative AI in their YU work. It covers data input bans, accuracy and bias checks, disclosure, research use, vendors, training, monitoring and review. It is not about student coursework.
documents.stance_why: The document sets conduct rules for faculty and staff, not a stance on student AI use. It "supports responsible experimentation with generative AI tools by its faculty and staff" under conditions and gives only general guidance for instruction, so no student-facing stance is set and the stance is delegates.

units.anchor: Generative AI tools have the capacity to expedite existing processes and make possible new ones

units.anchor: the risk that the output may be biased, misleading, or inaccurate

units.anchor: Generative AI has made it easier for malicious actors to create sophisticated phishing emails

units.anchor: the technology may not respect the privacy rights of individuals

units.anchor: the University may lose its intellectual property (IP) rights to that information

documents.title: Academic Integrity Policy: Resources (syllabus language)
documents.summary: Integrity-office resources page with four syllabus templates for AI use, advice on written and electronic assessments, and a Turn-it-in screening threshold. It says generative AI is not permitted in most classes unless explicitly allowed.
documents.stance_why: The page offers four templates (assistive only, select generative, all allowed, none allowed) and says "faculty should adjust the templates as needed", so by the tier/template rule the stance is delegates. It also says "in most classes, the use of generative artificial intelligence is not permitted", a restrictive background default.

notes: Coded independently (Coder A). The UG policy PDF is dated August 2026 and still has "[DATE]" for its effective date. The AUP is internal and covers faculty and staff, so its units are mostly P50, P52, P62, P65. The resources page is partial; electronic-exam proctoring tips (Proctorio, seating) were skipped because they do not mention AI. No school or computing-unit policy found.
